newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NSW Australia barley pool prices rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NSW Australia barley pool prices rise.

text.p: Farmers should expect increases of between A$5.00 and A$10.00 a tonne for Number One-grade Malt Barley because of strong early sales, the New South Wales Grains Board (NSWGB) said on Monday.
The increases would lift net pool returns for number one malt barley to as much as A$232.00 a tonne from the current A$222.00 a tonne, the board said.
"For malt barley 2/3 grades, good sales to date also resulted (in) a forecast increase in the net pool return by A$5.00-A$10.00 a tonne to up to A$200.00 a tonne from A$185.00," it said.

Very high feed pool return forecasts are expected to hold firm at A$175.00 a tonne based on current sales, about A$30.00 a tonne higher than those of the Australian Barley Board (ABB) in Victoria and South Australia, it said.

Managing director Graham Lawrence said the NSWGB had been able to command price premiums from international customers. This had been passed on through higher returns to growers delivering to NSWGB pools, he said.

Growers delivering to NSWGB malting barley pools had received more than A$20.00 a tonne premium on ABB Victorian number one malt barley, despite more difficult delivery requirements in Victoria, he said.
NSWGB prices had over the past five years had averaged A$17.00 a tonne more than other Australian statutory marketing bodies, he said.

China was a key market for the NSWGB for malt barley. Japan was a key feed barley market while Middle Eastern countries such as Saudi Arabia and Kuwait were also establishing themselves as significant customers of the NSWGB and now accounted for more
than 20 percent of its grain exports, he said.
Demand for feed barley in Arabic countries was steadily increasing and would result in continued growth for NSW feed barley exports, he said.
